estimates.subject: Active Energy Performance Contracts in EU-27, approximately 2024
estimates.methodNotes: Two independent methods: (A) EUROACE revenue bottom-up: EUR 3-5B market revenue / EUR 500K-5M average project value = 600-10,000 active contracts. (B) BPIE cumulative top-down: 35,000+ cumulative projects / assumed 5-year average active duration ≈ 7,000 active. Methods agree on central tendency ~2,000-7,000. Lower bound 2,000 conservative (large projects, short active window). Upper bound 10,000 (smaller projects, longer active window). No point estimate offered — range is the honest output.

assumptions.assumption: Average EPC project value: EUR 500K-5M (10x range — dominant sensitivity)
Average EPC active M&V period: 3-7 years (IPMVP standard)
EUROACE revenue coverage: 70-90% of actual EU ESCO market

estimates.precedenceRule: Both methods consistent. Triangulated range preferred. If methods diverged >3×, investigate definitions.

witnessInferenceGuard.reason: No WITNESS evidence. Estimate derived from industry association revenue data.

estimates.notes: This is the key denominator for DOGFOOD A. Average project value assumption dominates. Decision boundary: even the lower bound (2,000 EPCs) is a tractable beachhead for early-stage product without requiring high market share.

estimates.subject: Active EPC engagements EU-27 (BPIE cumulative method counter-estimate)
estimates.methodNotes: BPIE: 35,000+ cumulative ESCO projects EU since 2000. 26-year period. Steady-state assumption: ~1,350/year new projects. At 5-year average active M&V period → 6,750 active. Range: 3-7 year duration → 4,050-9,450.

assumptions.assumption: Uniform project start rate since 2000 (not realistic — growth accelerating post-2015)

estimates.notes: Counter-estimate to est-a02-eligible-count. Used in triangulation. Both methods consistent.

estimates.subject: Annual EPC M&V settlement disputes in EU-27
estimates.methodNotes: Dispute rate is completely unknown. No public statistic exists. IPMVP body does not publish dispute rate. Upper bound on annual dispute events = active EPCs (est-a02) × 1 settlement/year = 2,000-10,000. But this assumes 100% dispute rate — implausible. True rate unknown. Lower bound = 0 (implausible given existence of M&V verifier market at EUR 5K-50K/engagement). Decision boundary: at 10% rate → 200-1,000 dispute events/year. At 30% → 600-3,000/year. Strategic decision does not require knowing exact rate if even the low scenario is commercially viable.

witnessInferenceGuard.reason: Zero WITNESS evidence. TERRAIN status = HYPOTHESIS. Dispute rate cannot be inferred from AI_HYPOTHESIS alone. This is the most important unknown for DOGFOOD A.

estimates.notes: HIGHEST-VALUE UNKNOWN for DOGFOOD A. Next measurement: EUROACE member survey on M&V dispute rate OR extract from EED national reports.

estimates.subject: Annual high-stakes B2B procurement decision events, EU-27 manufacturing+regulated
estimates.methodNotes: est-b02 (50,000 enterprises) × assumed 2-10 qualifying events/enterprise/year. Lower: 50,000 × 2 = 100,000. Upper: 50,000 × 10 = 500,000. The events/enterprise/year assumption has HIGH sensitivity and no public source. This is an EXPLORATORY range. Including NACE J+M partial contribution would expand upper bound to ~650,000 but also increases overlap risk with SaaS review platforms.

estimates.subject: Registered grid flexibility sites EU-27+UK, ~2024
estimates.methodNotes: Method A (ENTSO-E capacity): FCR ~3,000 MW EU contracted / average site 1-5 MW → 600-3,000 (TSO markets only, lower bound). Method B (aggregator-based): ACER 200+ aggregators × 10-50 sites/aggregator → 2,000-10,000 (includes DSO estimate). Methods overlap in 2,000-3,000 range. Lower bound 600 is minimum observable from TSO data alone. Upper bound 10,000 includes DSO flexibility not captured in ENTSO-E. Preferred pre-download range: 2,000-5,000.

assumptions.assumption: Average flexibility site capacity: 1-5 MW (dominant sensitivity for Method A, unobserved)
Average sites per aggregator: 10-50 (dominant sensitivity for Method B, unobserved)
ENTSO-E FCR data is representative of TSO-managed flexibility sites

estimates.precedenceRule: Both methods consistent in central range 2,000-5,000. Discrepancy at extremes due to DSO coverage gap in ENTSO-E. Method B preferred as upper bound.

witnessInferenceGuard.reason: No WITNESS evidence. Estimate derived from capacity data and aggregator count proxy.

estimates.notes: NEXT MEASUREMENT: Download ENTSO-E BSP register to count registered Balancing Service Providers. This would narrow the range from 5× to likely 2×. High information value, zero cost, available now.
